record.paper_title: Grothendieck’s inequality and completely correlation preserving functions - a summary of recent results and an indication of related research problems
record.original_question: For the real and complex fields F in {R, C}, determine the exact numerical values of the Grothendieck constants K_G^R and K_G^C, where K_G^F is the least constant K for which every finite matrix (a_ij) over F and every choice of unit vectors u_i and v_j in an F-Hilbert space satisfy |Σ_i Σ_j a_ij ⟨u_i, v_j⟩| ≤ K sup{|Σ_i Σ_j a_ij p_i q_j| : |p_i| = |q_j| = 1}. If exact values cannot yet be obtained, develop methods that approximate K_G^R and K_G^C from above and below using the paper’s proposed framework of block matrix analysis, Gaussian random vectors, special functions, copulas, and combinatorics.

evidence.quote: The smallest possible value of the corresponding constant K is called the Grothendieck constant K F G. The superscripts R and C are used to indicate the different values in the real and complex case.

Computing the exact numerical value of the constants K R G and K C G is still an open problem (unsolved since 1953). Here, our own research activities are attached. We look for a general framework (primarily build on methods originating from (block) matrix analysis, multivariate statistics with real and complex Gaussian random vectors, theory of special functions, modelling of statistical dependence with copulas and combinatorics, whose complexity increases rapidly in dimension, though) which allows us either to give the value of K R G, respectively K C G explicitly or to approximate these values from above and from below at least.

Apart from its comprehensive mathematical fascination and richness the highly fascinating open problem of determining the value of the both Grothendieck constants K R G and K C G meanwhile is deeply linked with different fields, even including applications in computer science, high-dimensional data analyis and quantum mechanics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}\in\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}\}$. The Grothendieck constant $K_G^{\mathbb{F}}$ is defined as the smallest constant $K\in[1,\infty)$ such that, for every positive integer $n$, every matrix $(a_{ij})_{i,j=1}^n$ with entries in $\mathbb{F}$, every Hilbert space $H$ over $\mathbb{F}$, and every choice of unit vectors $u_1,\dots,u_n,v_1,\dots,v_n\in H$,
$$\Bigl|\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}\langle u_i,v_j\rangle\Bigr|\;\le\;K\,\sup\Bigl\{\Bigl|\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}p_iq_j\Bigr|\;:\;p_i,q_j\in\mathbb{F},\;|p_i|=|q_j|=1\Bigr\}.$$
Determine the exact numerical values of $K_G^{\mathbb{R}}$ and $K_G^{\mathbb{C}}$. If exact values are not attainable, provide rigorous upper and lower bounds approximating them, e.g. via methods of block matrix analysis, Gaussian random vectors, special functions, copulas, and combinatorics.
artifact.status_search_result: The exact values of the real and complex Grothendieck constants have been an open problem since Grothendieck's 1953 résumé. Sharp upper and lower bounds are known (e.g., Krivine's bound and the Braverman–Makarychev–Makarychev–Naor improvement showing $K_G^{\mathbb{R}}$ is strictly less than Krivine's bound), but the exact values remain unknown as of recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Grothendieck inequality - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The exact value of the Grothendieck constants K_G^R and K_G^C are unknown.
status_evidence.claim: Exact values of both Grothendieck constants remain unknown.

status_evidence.title: The Grothendieck constant is strictly smaller than Krivine's bound (Braverman, Makarychev, Makarychev, Naor)
status_evidence.snippet: We prove that the real Grothendieck constant K_G^R is strictly less than pi/(2 ln(1+sqrt(2))).
status_evidence.claim: Improved bounds exist but exact value not determined.
